title: Relocated finite-machine call
statement: Let $C$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $C.k$ work tapes, let $en$ and $ex$ be states of $C$, and let $\iota$ be an injection from the $1+C.k$ tapes of its virtual-host simulation into $k$ ambient tapes. Suppose that, on empty input and starting with $\mathrm{stateWord}(C.k,\mathrm{arg})$ on its work tapes in state $en$, the machine reaches the configuration with work tapes $\mathrm{stateWord}(C.k,\mathrm{result})$ in state $ex$ after $t$ steps, and its state is never $ex$ at any earlier time $s<t$. For any ambient tape contents and head positions, Boolean words $\mathrm{arg}$ and $\mathrm{result}$, Boolean input word $x$, valid input-head position $p$, and output word $\mathrm{out}$, the embedded virtual-host simulation started from the corresponding configuration with tag true reaches the corresponding configuration based on the state-$ex$ result after $t$ steps; at every earlier time $s<t$, its state is not $(ex,\mathrm{true})$.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
An injection embeds the $1+C.k$ virtual-host tapes into $k$ ambient tapes
Ambient tape contents and head positions are arbitrary
Argument and result are Boolean words
The base machine reaches the specified state-$ex$ configuration after $t$ steps
The base machine's state is never $ex$ at any earlier time $s<t$
$p$ is a valid input-head position for $x$
The initial output word is arbitrary
